notes.meaning: God pronounces sorrow and judgment against Jerusalem. Though the city was called to be holy, it had become filthy with sin, openly rebellious toward God, and cruel to its own people.

Jerusalem stubbornly refused to listen to God's warnings through His prophets or learn from His discipline. Instead of trusting in the Lord and drawing near to Him in prayer, she drifted away and put her confidence in human help.

The rulers of the city acted like dangerous wild animals toward their own people. The princes used their power to tear citizens apart like roaring lions, and greedy judges devoured everything in sight without leaving even a bone for morning.

The religious leaders were just as ungodly as the rulers. False prophets treated their sacred duties lightly and betrayed the people's trust, while the priests made God's holy temple unclean and twisted His law for their own ends.

Even though the people were wicked, the Lord remained in their midst and did no wrong. Every morning He showed His perfect justice and never failed, yet the unrighteous people felt no shame at all for their bad behavior.

God reminded Jerusalem of how He had brought down foreign nations, breaking their strong corner towers and leaving their streets completely empty. He hoped Judah would take warning, learn reverent fear, and accept His discipline so her homes would not be ruined. Instead, the people could not wait to get out of bed early in the morning just to rush into more sin.

The Lord tells the faithful to wait patiently until the day He rises to carry out His judgment. He plans to gather kingdoms from all over the earth to pour His anger upon evil, showing His deep passion to protect His holy name and purify the world.

After the judgment, God promises to purify the speech and hearts of the nations. Cleansed from worshiping idols, people everywhere will call on the Lord and work together in true unity, pulling side by side like oxen under one yoke.

differ.view: This promise began at Pentecost and is being fulfilled in the church age as people of all tongues hear the gospel, receive clean hearts, and worship God together.
This looks ahead to a future thousand-year earthly reign of Christ after His return, when all surviving nations will turn to God and may even speak one pure, shared language.

notes.meaning: True worshipers will bring gifts to the Lord from the farthest reaches of the known earth, beyond the headwaters of the Nile River in Africa. God promises that even His scattered people living in distant lands will return to offer Him worship.

On that coming day, God's people will no longer be overwhelmed with shame over their past sins, because the Lord will forgive them. He will clear away the arrogant hypocrites who boasted in the temple, so no one will ever act proud on His holy mountain again.

The Lord will leave behind a remnant, which is a small surviving group of faithful believers. These people are meek, poor in spirit, and fully aware of their weakness, so they put all their trust in the name of the Lord rather than in themselves.

This purified remnant will refuse to practice injustice or speak dishonest words. Safe in the Lord's care, they will rest in peace and plenty like sheep in a quiet pasture, with no enemy or corrupt ruler left to make them afraid.
God commands His people to sing, shout, and celebrate with their whole hearts. Repeating the call to rejoice three times emphasizes that an overflowing, unsurpassed joy is in store for Jerusalem.

The Lord removes the punishment that their sins brought upon them and drives away their foes. With God Himself living among them as their true King and protector, they will never have to live in fear of ruin again.

A message of comfort will be spoken to Jerusalem, urging the people not to be terrified. Letting one's hands drop means losing heart and giving up, so they are encouraged to stay strong and keep doing the Lord's work.

The Lord is present with His people as a mighty Savior who conquers their foes and rescues them from sin. He takes deep delight in them, calming their fears with His resting love and rejoicing over them with loud songs of joy.

While in exile, faithful believers grieved because they could no longer gather at the temple for the sacred festival days. The Lord promises to bring these sorrowing worshipers home and lift the burden of shame that their enemies piled on them.

God will judge and punish every enemy who harmed His people. He will gently rescue those who are weak or injured, gather the exiles who were scattered into foreign lands, and turn their past disgrace into praise and honor across the whole earth.

The Lord repeats His sure promise to gather His people and lead them back to their home. They will see this great rescue with their very own eyes, and He will give them a honored name among all nations, for the Lord Himself has spoken it.
